definitions: To state that one refuses to admit the truth of something.
examples: The suspect chose to deny all charges made against him today.
She denied that the company had broken the contract.

definitions: To demand or assert something forcefully without accepting refusal or objection.
examples: My parents insist that I finish my homework before watching television.
She insisted that she was innocent.
He insisted on paying for the dinner.

definitions: To put forward an idea, plan, or proposal for consideration.
examples: I suggest taking the morning train to avoid heavy traffic delays.
I suggest meeting at six.
She suggested taking the train.

definitions: To advise or suggest something as a good or suitable choice.
examples: The waiter recommended trying the fresh seafood pasta special tonight.
Can you recommend a good hotel?
I recommend this book to everyone.

definitions: To inform someone in advance of a possible danger or problem.
examples: Forecasters warn residents that a severe storm will arrive tonight.
Warn children about the hot stove.
The guard warned us about ice.

definitions: To cause someone to lose confidence or enthusiasm for an action.
examples: Bad weather might discourage people from attending the outdoor concert.

definitions: To offer suggestions or counsel to someone about the best course.
examples: Doctors advise drinking plenty of fresh water throughout hot summer days.
I would advise you to wait until tomorrow.

definitions: To give someone facts or information in a formal or official manner.
examples: Please inform us immediately if your travel plans change next week.
Inform us if your plans change.
The letter informed him of the date.

definitions: To make a public or official statement about a fact or event.
examples: The principal will announce the winner of the competition tomorrow morning.
Announce the test results on Monday.
The airline announced a delay.

definitions: To tell someone something positively to dispel any doubts they hold.
examples: The manager assured us that the project would finish on time.
I assure you that everything will be fine.
The doctor assured us that he would recover.

definitions: To say or do something to remove the doubts and fears of.
examples: She tried to reassure her worried friend before the big exam.

definitions: To indicate or show that one is not willing to do something.
examples: He had to refuse the invitation because of a prior commitment.
He refused to sign the contract without legal advice.

definitions: To consent to a proposal, condition, or course of action suggested.
examples: The company agreed to lower the price for their loyal customers.

definitions: To express disapproval or opposition to a plan, action, or idea.
examples: Local residents object to building a commercial parking lot nearby.

definitions: To express an opinion or remark about a particular topic or event.
examples: The minister declined to comment on the ongoing police investigation.

definitions: To say or write something as a reaction to a question.
examples: Please respond to the invitation email before Friday afternoon at five.
I asked him a question but he didn't respond.
The government responded to the crisis quickly.

definitions: To answer or respond in words or writing to a message.
examples: She promised to reply to my message as soon as possible.
He always replies to emails the same day.

definitions: To act in response to something; show a physical or emotional reaction.
examples: How did he react when he heard the exciting promotion news?
How did he react to the news?

definitions: To succeed in doing or completing something.
examples: She worked hard to accomplish all her goals for the year.
They accomplished the task ahead of schedule.
Setting goals helps you accomplish more.

definitions: To say that someone has done something wrong or illegal.
examples: He was wrong to accuse his colleague without any proof.
He was falsely accused of taking the keys.
Do not accuse others without clear proof.

definitions: To gain or obtain something for oneself.
examples: Students can acquire new skills through regular practice.
Students acquire new language skills quickly.
The company acquired a smaller firm.

definitions: To make or become different; modify.
examples: We had to alter our travel plans due to bad weather.
She altered her dress to fit better.
Nothing can alter the final result.

definitions: To officially agree to or accept a proposal or decision.
examples: The committee will approve the budget proposal next week.
The city council approved the budget.
My manager approved my vacation leave.

definitions: To give official permission for something.
examples: Only the manager can authorize access to these files.

definitions: To help something increase, improve, or become successful.
examples: Regular exercise can boost your energy levels significantly.
Good publicity boosted ticket sales.
Coffee boosts energy in the morning.

definitions: To give an authoritative order to someone.
examples: The officer commanded the soldiers to halt immediately.

definitions: To hide something or prevent it from being seen.
examples: He tried to conceal his anxiety behind a cheerful smile.
The report concealed several significant conflicts of interest.

definitions: To face up to and deal with a problem or difficult situation.
examples: You need to confront your fears rather than run away.
She confronted the difficult issue at the board meeting.

definitions: To change the form, character, or function of something.
examples: They decided to convert the old barn into a modern home.

definitions: To protect from harm, attack, or criticism.
examples: She stood up to defend her friend from unfair claims.

definitions: To completely remove or get rid of something.
examples: The new policy aims to eliminate unnecessary paperwork.

definitions: To make something visible or uncovered.
examples: Investigative journalists helped expose the hidden truth.
The investigation exposed widespread financial misconduct.

definitions: To obtain or win something desirable.
examples: You will gain valuable experience by working abroad.

definitions: To manage, deal with, or control a situation.
examples: She knows how to handle difficult customer complaints.

definitions: To keep something in good condition or at the same level.
examples: It is important to maintain good health through exercise.
She maintained that her decision was based entirely on evidence.

definitions: To make small changes to something to improve it.
examples: You can modify the document settings to fit your needs.

definitions: To observe and check the progress or quality of something.
examples: Doctors will monitor the patient's condition closely.

definitions: To behave as if something is true when you know it is not.
examples: Children often pretend to be superheroes while playing.

definitions: To refuse to accept, use, or believe something.
examples: The publisher decided to reject the initial manuscript draft.

definitions: To take something away from a place or position.
examples: Please remove your shoes before entering the house.
Please remove your shoes.
They removed the old furniture.

definitions: To take the place of something or substitute another thing.
examples: We need to replace the broken light bulb in the hallway.
The new software will replace the old system next year.

definitions: To limit the size, amount, or freedom of something.
examples: The rule will restrict parking on main streets during peak hours.
Access to the building is restricted to badge holders only.

definitions: To make or become stronger.
examples: Regular practice will strengthen your language skills.

definitions: To use or add someone or something in place of another.
examples: You can substitute honey for sugar in this cake recipe.

definitions: To make determined efforts to deal with a problem.
examples: The government plans to tackle environmental issues this year.

definitions: To make or become less strong or influential.
examples: Lack of sleep can weaken your immune system over time.

definitions: To finish making, doing, or filling out something entirely.
examples: Be sure to complete all sections of your visa registration form accurately before submitting.
Please complete the application form.
He completed the race in record time.

definitions: to follow or strive to achieve a goal, career path, or study course
examples: She decided to relocate abroad to pursue a master's degree in business administration.
He pursued his ambition of running his own business.

definitions: to strive or make strenuous efforts in the face of difficulties or opposition
examples: Newcomers may struggle initially with rapid spoken dialects before gaining language confidence.

definitions: give someone or something the authority or means to do something
examples: Securing a residence permit enables newcomers to open local bank accounts and lease apartments.
The new technology enables remote teams to collaborate better.

definitions: give a summary or general description of something
examples: The guide outlines key steps required when applying for a permanent residency permit.

definitions: identify clearly and definitely in detail
examples: The lease agreement must specify the monthly rental fee and utility responsibilities.

definitions: to take a brief, hurried look at someone or something for a split second
examples: She glanced at her watch nervously while waiting for the train to arrive.

definitions: to walk in a relaxed, leisurely way for pleasure or exercise
examples: Families frequently stroll along the beachfront promenade on sunny Sunday afternoons.

definitions: To spend an extravagant amount of money on a luxury.
examples: We saved money on cheap lunches so we could splurge on a fine dinner.

definitions: To ask for something urgently or authoritatively as a right or necessity.
examples: Workers gathered outside headquarters to demand better working conditions.

definitions: A general plan or summary showing the main features of a topic or project.
examples: The teacher provided a detailed outline of the course topics.

definitions: To turn something aside, changing its direction or redirecting public focus.
examples: The politician tried to deflect attention from his economic failures by organizing a giant athletic parade.

definitions: Get rid of someone or something as no longer useful or desirable.
examples: Farms are often forced to discard nearly forty percent of their harvest.

definitions: To strike means to hit someone or something.
examples: Do not strike the animal.
The ball struck the window.

definitions: To fire a gun means to shoot it.
examples: The guard fired a warning shot.
Soldiers must not fire without an order.

definitions: To tap means to knock something lightly.
examples: She tapped the window to get attention.
He tapped his fingers on the table.
